bullets.text: Companywide CR was 91.9; PL CR improved 10.9 pts YOY to 88.6; CL CR improved 7.8 pts YOY to 88.6, with TNC better than target; Property CR was 166.3.
Companywide NPW grew 22% YOY; Personal Lines NPW increased 26% to $14.6 billion, reflecting robust new application growth; Property NPW grew 11%; Commercial Lines NPW rose 6%.
Companywide PIF +9% YOY; PL ended with nearly 28M PIFs, adding 1.1M auto policies in Q2 (2M in 1H, an estimated 3.4M cars); Property PIF rose 12% to over 3.3M; CL PIF +1%.

Property weather losses added 76 pts to Q2 CR (48 pts YTD); reinsurance retention threshold was nearly reached under the aggregate storm program; hurricane contract provides $2.0B coverage excess of $200M retention.
Personal auto frequency declined 8% YOY, and severity was relatively flat; 2023 rate increases continued earning in; May was the most active month for severe weather in 13 years.

Progressive moderated rate increases and continued unwinding 2023 non-rate restrictions, implementing small rate decreases in eight states; Property rates rose ~4% in Q2 (~17% trailing 12 months); commercial auto competitors aggressively took rate.

Debt-to-total capital dropped to 22.8%, lowest since February 2022; no bond maturities until 2027; portfolio FTE total return was 0.9% (equity 3.6%, fixed income 0.8%); portfolio duration was extended to 3.2 years.

Auto product model 8.9 reached eight states (16% PIF); commercial auto rolled its newest model to two states; BOP was in 46 states, including 22 on the newest model; multi-product agent quoting piloted.

Non-acquisition expense ratio decreased 0.3 points YOY in first-half 2024; increased advertising spend and unwinding non-rate restrictions resulted in record second-quarter quote and new application volumes across Agency and Direct channels.

Customer-turned-employee Dannielle shared how claims compassion after her son’s tragic car accident inspired her career on the Customer Preservation Team; people and culture continue serving Progressive and customers well.
